newsitem.title: CANADA: PRESS DIGEST - Canada - Wednesday, July 16, 1997.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Canada - Wednesday, July 16, 1997.

text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-EU opening door to East: Five ex-Communist countries, plus Cyprus, to be recommended for membership today
-Future of SFU president in doubt: Review possible in harassment case
-Canada may be tied to U.S. probe: Political fund-raising investigation could link Huang to cross-border soliciting
-Police name suspect in killing of Versace: Fashion designer shot in Miami Beach
-Fund-raising job for members only: Part-time Ontario telephone solicitors pressured to join Reform Party
-Bear pulls boy from tent: Rangers lay traps in Algonquin Park
-Mutual fund assets set record: Soaring stock markets, fresh cash send total surging to $258-billion by end of June
-World events batter oil, gas stocks: Volatility hits Canadian sector again
-U.S. renews Helms-Burton waiver: Disallows lawsuits against firms on expropriated Cuban land
-Former penny stock salesman exposes manipulative methods: Client had 'no chance of making money'
-Mutual funds' surge prompts warning: Fund asset growth for the first half of 1997 is already ahead of forecasts for the whole year, but some analysts are concerned
-Steel sector on a roll as Ipsco earnings soar
